q: For a mutual fund return calculation over a holding period of more than one year, the appropriate measure is:
e: CAGR = (End/Begin)^(1/n) − 1. The standard return measure for periods ≥ 1 year. Absolute return is used for < 1 year periods. XIRR is used for SIPs (irregular cash flows).

q: Returns from a SIP are best calculated using:
e: SIP cash flows are irregular (multiple installments at different times + final redemption). XIRR computes the IRR for these irregular flows. Most fund factsheets show both lump-sum CAGR and SIP XIRR.

q: Tracking Error of an index fund measures:
o: How closely the scheme's returns track the benchmark — lower is better
e: Tracking Error = standard deviation of (Scheme return − Benchmark return). Lower TE = the scheme tracks its benchmark closely. Causes of TE: cash holdings, expenses, rebalancing lag.

q: Sharpe Ratio uses which measure of risk in the denominator?
e: Sharpe = (Rp − Rf) / σ_p, using the portfolio's total standard deviation. Treynor uses beta and is more suited for well-diversified portfolios where unsystematic risk is gone.

o: It moves 20% less than its benchmark
It moves 20% more than its benchmark (more volatile)
It is uncorrelated with the benchmark
e: β = 1.2 means the scheme is approximately 20% more volatile than its benchmark. β = 1: moves with benchmark; β < 1: less volatile (defensive); β > 1: more volatile (aggressive).

q: Which of these is a SEBI-mandated past-performance disclaimer?
o: Past performance is a guarantee of future returns
Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future
Past returns indicate exact future performance
e: SEBI mandates the disclaimer 'Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future' on every MF advertisement. Distributors must NOT use past performance as the sole selling point.

q: Rolling returns are preferred over point-to-point returns because:
o: They remove the dependency on start and end dates
They are mandated by SEBI only
They show only the best returns
e: Rolling returns compute CAGR over many overlapping windows (e.g. 3-year rolling). This removes the bias of cherry-picked start/end dates and shows return consistency, not luck of timing.

o: Manager's active outperformance per unit of tracking error
e: Information Ratio = (Rp − Rb) / Tracking Error. Measures how efficiently a manager generates excess return over benchmark per unit of active risk. Higher = better active management.

q: AMCs must publish daily NAV by what time?
e: Daily NAV must be disclosed by 11 PM on the AMC + AMFI websites. This ensures investors and applicants have current pricing for next-day decisions.
